clue.text: Quit out-of-control press about one scandalous reporter

parts.note: to go is to quit or leave

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, or around, the numeral
letters that are out of control run wild into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tabloid hack spreads scandal after quitting a press office that has spun out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers, fitting a reporter, but it is only anagram fodder; 'out-of-control' gives SSPER, which 'about' wraps round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who spreads scandal is a tattler, passing on rumour and tittle-tattle.

clue.text: After one sees shape of egg, change egg supplier

explanation.walkthrough: 'After one sees' is just link padding: O is followed by VARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The female organ that produces ova is the body's own source of eggs.

clue.text: Perhaps vampire slayer's assistant who has a real interest

a person with a genuine investment or concern in an enterprise

explanation.definitionFit: An investor or party with a share in a business outcome; also, literally, whoever holds the wooden spike.

clue.text: Very inadequate way evidence is brought up

explanation.walkthrough: 'is brought up' turns CITE upwards to ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitifully feeble or woefully poor is described colloquially as pathetic.

clue.text: Sought treasures for puzzling treatment in this?

clue.text: Mostly plain youth finds romance

clue.text: Close to hypotenuse, for example

clue.text: Empty tin into large tank

clue.text: Stamp fifty pence pieces?

explanation.definitionFit: Stamp means kind or sort; printers' metal letters collectively are also called by this word.

clue.text: Unfortunately gloomy tone in which cricket may be studied

clue.text: Old streetwalker is comparatively weak, without promise
